title: A View of the Beginning of Time: An Update

sentences.en: 33 presidents.
sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.en: I called the president at 4.30 in the morning and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我在凌晨4点半给总统打了电话，他接听了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 太空探索的七十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗恒星之外有什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 一千份消费品指南。

sentences.en: Today I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天我正在测试七款床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60份超级圣代。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 他们可能每年都是联盟里最强的球队。

sentences.en: 53,500 puzzles.
I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都用不同的起始词。

sentences.en: 25,000 recipes.
And I love a one pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢一锅出的食谱，因为我不喜欢洗锅。

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》，庆祝175年来致力于帮助您了解世界并充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 立即订阅，获取nytimes.com/subscribe的特别优惠。

sentences.en: Hey, it's Michael.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是迈克尔。

sentences.en: All this week, The Daily is revisiting some of our favorite episodes of the year and learning what's happened in the time since they first ran.
sentences.zh: 整个这一周，《每日新闻》都在回顾我们今年最喜欢的一些剧集，并了解它们首次播出后发生了什么。

sentences.en: Today, we return to an episode hosted by my colleague,
sentences.zh: 今天，我们回到由我同事主持的一期节目，

sentences.en: Estet Herndon, about the incredible moment when the James Webb Telescope, the largest space observatory ever built, sent its first images back to Earth
sentences.zh: 埃斯特·赫恩登（Estet Herndon），讲述了詹姆斯·韦伯望远镜——有史以来建造的最大的太空观测站——将第一批图像传回地球的不可思议时刻，

sentences.en: and hear what it's discovered since then in its long journey across the universe.
sentences.zh: 并听听它在穿越宇宙的漫长旅程中发现了什么。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, December 28th.
sentences.zh: 今天是12月28日，星期三。

sentences.en: So Ken, there was big news in space this week.
sentences.zh: 那么肯，这周太空领域有大新闻。

sentences.en: Can you tell us about these new pictures from NASA that were revealed?
sentences.zh: 你能给我们讲讲NASA公布的这些新照片吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, we finally got pictures back from the James Webb Space Telescope.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们终于收到了詹姆斯·韦伯太空望远镜传回的照片。

sentences.en: This is the biggest, newest telescope that NASA has.
sentences.zh: 这是NASA拥有最大、最新的望远镜。

sentences.en: So these first photographs from Webb were so amazing that on Monday...
sentences.zh: 所以韦伯传回的第一批照片太令人惊叹了，以至于在周一……

sentences.en: Six and a half months ago, a rocket launched from Earth carrying the world's newest, most powerful deep space telescope.
sentences.zh: 六个半月前，一枚火箭从地球发射升空，携带了世界上最新、最强大的深空望远镜。

sentences.en: President Biden had a special event to unveil their very first photograph.
sentences.zh: 拜登总统举办了一场特别活动，揭开了它们的第一张照片。

sentences.en: These images are going to remind the world that America can do big things.
sentences.zh: 这些图像将提醒全世界，美国能够成就伟大的事业。

sentences.en: And one of the things they saw was a galaxy where it's so far away that the light took more than 13 billion years to get to us here on Earth.
sentences.zh: 他们看到的其中一件事是一个星系，它距离我们如此遥远，以至于光线花了超过130亿年的时间才到达地球。

sentences.en: Light where stars were born and from where they die.
sentences.zh: 那是恒星诞生和消亡的光芒。

sentences.en: The universe is 13.8 billion years, so, you know, it's going way back.
sentences.zh: 宇宙有138亿年的历史，所以，你知道，这追溯到了很久以前。

sentences.en: Let's do it.
sentences.zh: 我们开始吧。

sentences.en: Okay, we've got the whole world watching.
sentences.zh: 好的，全世界都在关注。

sentences.en: Are you ready to put the first image up?
sentences.zh: 你准备好展示第一张图像了吗？

sentences.en: Oh, let's do it.
sentences.zh: 哦，我们开始吧。

sentences.en: Let's do it.
sentences.zh: 我们开始吧。

sentences.en: And then on Tuesday, NASA had a separate event to show four other photographs.
sentences.zh: 然后在周二，NASA举办了另一场活动，展示了另外四张照片。

sentences.en: Okay, Amber, so here it is.
sentences.zh: 好的，安珀，就是这张。

sentences.en: Can you walk us through the final...
sentences.zh: 你能带我们看看最后一张……

sentences.en: And they're just gorgeous.
sentences.zh: 它们简直太美了。

sentences.en: There was an amazing photograph of this stellar nursery.
sentences.zh: 有一张令人惊叹的恒星托儿所照片。

sentences.en: You could see all these ripples of gas where new stars are being born.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到所有这些气体涟漪，新恒星正在那里诞生。

sentences.en: You could see another picture of a dying star, another one of five galaxies are in this intricate gravitational dance.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到另一张垂死恒星的照片，还有一张是五个星系正在进行复杂的引力之舞。

sentences.en: Okay, so the first image is a deep field.
sentences.zh: 好的，第一张图像是一个深场。

sentences.en: And it's also a deep field with a cluster.
sentences.zh: 它也是一个带有星团的深场。

sentences.en: So this is what they call a deep field, which is basically point a telescope at a relatively empty part of the sky and see what's out there.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们所说的深场，基本上就是把望远镜对准天空中相对空旷的部分，看看那里有什么。

sentences.en: There are galaxies here in which you're seeing individual clusters of stars forming, popping up, just like popcorn.
sentences.zh: 这里有一些星系，你可以看到单个星团正在形成，像爆米花一样冒出来。

sentences.en: What's amazing is that you realize that the universe, you just look in the sky, it looks like it's mostly empty.
sentences.zh: 令人惊奇的是，你意识到宇宙——你只是抬头看天空，它看起来大部分是空的。

sentences.en: But once you look at it in these new wavelengths of light, you realize there's exciting structure.
sentences.zh: 但一旦你用这些新的光波长观察它，你就会意识到那里有令人兴奋的结构。

sentences.en: There's just a sharpness and a clarity we've never had.
sentences.zh: 有一种我们从未有过的清晰度和锐度。

sentences.en: Colors.
sentences.zh: 色彩。

sentences.en: Kind of littered like jewels all over the back of the image are these faint red galaxies.
sentences.zh: 图像背景上散落着这些微弱的红色星系，就像珠宝一样。

sentences.en: Things going on that you never realize until you put a telescope in space to look at them.
sentences.zh: 如果不把望远镜放到太空中去观察，你永远不会意识到正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: This is how the oxygen in our bodies was made in stars, in galaxies.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们体内的氧气是如何在恒星和星系中制造出来的。

sentences.en: And we're seeing that process get started.
sentences.zh: 我们正在见证这个过程的开始。

sentences.en: It is really kind of like wondrous.
sentences.zh: 这真的让人感到奇妙。

sentences.en: What was the scientific reaction to these images?
sentences.zh: 科学界对这些图像有什么反应？

sentences.en: The scientists kept on saying that they were speechless.
sentences.zh: 科学家们一直说他们说不出话来。

sentences.en: One person said that she ugly cried when she saw the first data.
sentences.zh: 有人说她在看到第一批数据时哭得很难看。

sentences.en: Someone was joking that all the astronomers in the world have changed their background screens on their computers yesterday.
sentences.zh: 有人开玩笑说，全世界的天文学家昨天都换了电脑背景屏幕。

sentences.en: So these are basically the very first efforts pointing the telescope at the very first few targets and not even trying very hard yet.
sentences.zh: 所以这些基本上是第一次尝试将望远镜对准最初的几个目标，甚至还没有怎么努力。

sentences.en: But this is basically just scratching the surface of what we'll be able to do in the coming years.
sentences.zh: 但这基本上只是触及了我们未来几年能够做到的事情的皮毛。

sentences.en: So tell us about the piece of technology that actually took these images.
sentences.zh: 那么告诉我们关于拍摄这些图像的技术设备吧。

sentences.en: This James Webb telescope sounds like space's newest, hottest invention.
sentences.zh: 这个詹姆斯·韦伯望远镜听起来像是太空领域最新、最热门的发明。

sentences.en: That's exactly what it is.
sentences.zh: 事实正是如此。

sentences.en: It's the successor to NASA's Hubble Space Telescope, which has been taking photographs of the universe for decades now.
sentences.zh: 它是NASA哈勃太空望远镜的继任者，哈勃几十年来一直在拍摄宇宙的照片。

sentences.en: James Webb is bigger.
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯·韦伯更大。

sentences.en: So that means it can gather much more light and see dimmer objects much farther away to almost the Big Bang.
sentences.zh: 这意味着它可以收集更多的光，看到更远、更暗的物体，几乎能看到大爆炸时期。

sentences.en: It's looking back to when the first stars and the first galaxies formed.
sentences.zh: 它正在回望第一批恒星和星系形成的时候。

sentences.en: And this is probably within a half billion years after the Big Bang, the very story of the universe.
sentences.zh: 这可能是在大爆炸后的五亿年内，也就是宇宙的起源故事。

sentences.en: You know, I don't want to say the words time travel, but it feels the closest to time travel we have.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我不想说“时间旅行”这个词，但它感觉是我们所拥有的最接近时间旅行的东西。

sentences.en: Astronomy really is time travel because light takes time to reach us.
sentences.zh: 天文学确实就是时间旅行，因为光到达我们需要时间。

sentences.en: The farther anything is, the longer it takes light to get to us.
sentences.zh: 物体越远，光到达我们这里所需的时间就越长。

sentences.en: So when we look at the farthest things, we are looking back in time.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们观察最遥远的事物时，我们就是在回望过去。

sentences.en: Okay, Ken.
sentences.zh: 好的，肯。

sentences.en: So let's go back in time.
sentences.zh: 那么让我们回到过去吧。

sentences.en: Tell us how this telescope came to be and how it became this defining moment for NASA.
sentences.zh: 告诉我们这个望远镜是如何诞生的，以及它是如何成为NASA这一决定性时刻的。

sentences.en: Back in 1990, NASA launched the Hubble Space Telescope, which has produced these amazing pictures of the universe that almost everyone has seen.
sentences.zh: 早在1990年，NASA发射了哈勃太空望远镜，它拍摄了几乎每个人都见过的那些令人惊叹的宇宙照片。

sentences.en: And it's a resounding success now.
sentences.zh: 现在它取得了巨大的成功。

sentences.en: But when it launched, it was a huge embarrassment for NASA.
sentences.zh: 但当它发射时，对NASA来说是一个巨大的尴尬。

sentences.en: In what way?
sentences.zh: 怎么说？

sentences.en: Well, once they started getting the first images back, all the images were blurry.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当他们开始收到第一批图像时，所有的图像都是模糊的。

sentences.en: And they started tweaking.
sentences.zh: 他们开始进行调整。

sentences.en: Maybe they thought they needed to adjust something.
sentences.zh: 也许他们认为需要调整什么东西。

sentences.en: But no matter what they did, the images were still blurry.
sentences.zh: 但无论他们做什么，图像仍然是模糊的。

sentences.en: And after enough investigation, they've discovered that the mirror had been ground to the wrong shape.
sentences.zh: 经过充分调查，他们发现镜片被磨成了错误的形状。

sentences.en: And it was only by a tiny little bit.
sentences.zh: 而且只差了那么一点点。

sentences.en: The mirror is eight feet wide.
sentences.zh: 镜片有八英尺宽。

sentences.en: And the edges were two microns too shallow.
sentences.zh: 边缘浅了两个微米。

sentences.en: Wish I knew what a micron meant to fully understand that sentence.
sentences.zh: 真希望我知道微米是什么意思，才能完全理解那句话。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: A piece of paper is 100 microns thick.
sentences.zh: 一张纸的厚度是100微米。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: This is even crazier than I expected.
sentences.zh: 这比我预想的还要疯狂。

sentences.en: So a piece of paper is 100 microns thick, and you said this mirror was two microns too shallow.
sentences.zh: 所以一张纸有100微米厚，而你说这个镜片浅了两个微米。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Over something that's eight feet wide.
sentences.zh: 在八英尺宽的物体上。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And that made such a huge impact in Hubble.
sentences.zh: 这对哈勃造成了如此巨大的影响。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It looked like the billions of dollars they spent on Hubble was a complete failure.
sentences.zh: 看起来他们在哈勃上花费的数十亿美元完全失败了。

sentences.en: And that was very embarrassing for NASA at the time.
sentences.zh: 那在当时对NASA来说非常尴尬。

sentences.en: And it took several years for NASA to come up with a fix.
sentences.zh: NASA花了几年时间才想出补救办法。

sentences.en: And so in 1993, the space shuttle went up to Hubble in orbit around Earth.
sentences.zh: 于是在1993年，航天飞机飞向了绕地球运行的哈勃。

sentences.en: And the astronauts could actually install this new equipment.
sentences.zh: 宇航员们实际上可以安装这些新设备。

sentences.en: And after that, all the images from Hubble were clear again.
sentences.zh: 在那之后，哈勃传回的所有图像又变得清晰了。

sentences.en: And everything that people were hoping for from Hubble then succeeded.
sentences.zh: 人们对哈勃的所有期望在那时都实现了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And with Hubble, NASA could send astronauts with a space shuttle to fix the probleMs.
sentences.zh: 有了哈勃，NASA可以派遣宇航员乘坐航天飞机去解决问题。

sentences.en: There was no such luxury with Webb.
sentences.zh: 但韦伯没有这样的奢侈条件。

sentences.en: Because Webb was bigger and because of its design, it had to be at super cold temperatures, which meant they had to put it at this point of space that's a million miles from Earth.
sentences.zh: 因为韦伯更大，而且由于它的设计，它必须处于超低温状态，这意味着他们必须把它放在距离地球一百万英里的太空位置。

sentences.en: So everything that was on Webb had to work the first time.
sentences.zh: 所以韦伯上的一切都必须第一次就成功运行。

sentences.en: There was not going to be a chance to try it again.
sentences.zh: 没有机会再试一次。

sentences.en: And that means you have to check everything and check again.
sentences.zh: 这意味着你必须检查一切，然后再检查一遍。

sentences.en: And testing to make sure everything works one time correctly takes a lot of time and takes a lot of money.
sentences.zh: 为了确保一切都能一次性正确运行而进行的测试需要花费大量的时间和金钱。

sentences.en: And that's where the Webb project kept on running into problems over the years.
sentences.zh: 这就是韦伯项目多年来不断遇到问题的地方。

sentences.en: So when NASA gave the green light to the space telescope in the mid-1990s, they thought it would cost $1.5 billion, maybe a little bit more than that.
sentences.zh: 所以当NASA在90年代中期为这个太空望远镜开绿灯时，他们认为它将耗资15亿美元，也许比这多一点点。

sentences.en: And they thought it would be ready for launch by 2007.
sentences.zh: 他们认为它到2007年就可以发射了。

sentences.en: They underestimated just how hard it was and just how many things they had to invent along the way.
sentences.zh: 他们低估了这项工作的难度，以及他们一路上需要发明多少东西。

sentences.en: Like what?
sentences.zh: 比如什么？

sentences.en: There were some major design challenges they had to solve.
sentences.zh: 他们必须解决一些重大的设计挑战。

sentences.en: The first is that this mirror is huge.
sentences.zh: 首先是这个镜片非常巨大。

sentences.en: Hubble's telescope was 8 feet.
sentences.zh: 哈勃的望远镜是8英尺。

sentences.en: Webb's telescope is 21 feet.
sentences.zh: 韦伯的望远镜是21英尺。

sentences.en: It's as big as a two-story building.
sentences.zh: 它像一栋两层楼的建筑那么大。

sentences.en: So the other problem that they had was that everything had to be really cold because even just the slightest bit of heat would blur the images.
sentences.zh: 所以他们面临的另一个问题是，一切都必须非常冷，因为哪怕是最轻微的热量也会使图像模糊。

sentences.en: And why is that?
sentences.zh: 为什么会这样？

sentences.en: So the James Webb telescope is designed to look at infrared light.
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯·韦伯望远镜旨在观察红外光。

sentences.en: Because the universe is expanding, the furthest objects, their light gets shifted to the longer wavelengths.
sentences.zh: 因为宇宙在膨胀，最遥远的物体，它们的光会被转移到更长的波长。

sentences.en: And in order to see them, you have to look in the infrared, the part of the spectrum that is redder than red.
sentences.zh: 为了看到它们，你必须观察红外线，也就是光谱中比红色更红的部分。

sentences.en: And more importantly, infrared light is easily distorted if there's any sources of heat around it.
sentences.zh: 更重要的是，如果周围有任何热源，红外光很容易发生畸变。

sentences.en: And that's what led to the decision to put the telescope a million miles from Earth.
sentences.zh: 这就是导致决定将望远镜放置在距离地球一百万英里远的地方的原因。

sentences.en: So none of the heat from the Earth's atmosphere can affect the Webb telescope because it's so far away.
sentences.zh: 所以地球大气层的热量都不会影响韦伯望远镜，因为它太远了。

sentences.en: The other thing it had to do is make sure that it stayed cold.
sentences.zh: 它必须做的另一件事是确保它保持低温。

sentences.en: It had to be about minus 380 degrees Fahrenheit.
sentences.zh: 它必须保持在华氏零下380度左右。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And to get it that cold, they had to build a sunshield, which is this big piece of fabric that's the size of a tennis court
sentences.zh: 为了达到那么低的温度，他们必须建造一个遮阳罩，这是一块网球场大小的大型织物，

sentences.en: that's blocking sunlight and keeping anything from warming up the telescope.
sentences.zh: 它可以阻挡阳光，防止任何东西加热望远镜。

sentences.en: So how do you fit something that's a two-story-high mirror, a tennis court-sized sunshield, and pack it in a rocket?
sentences.zh: 那么你如何把一个两层楼高的镜片、一个网球场大小的遮阳罩装进火箭里呢？

sentences.en: Because there's no rockets that big.
sentences.zh: 因为没有那么大的火箭。

sentences.en: And so they had to do something that was almost like origami.
sentences.zh: 所以他们不得不做一些几乎像折纸一样的事情。

sentences.en: They broke the mirror part into little smaller hexagons that stacked on each other.
sentences.zh: 他们把镜片部分拆成一个个较小的六边形，堆叠在一起。

sentences.en: They had to fold up the sunshield and pack that all into a rocket and design it so that once it's in space, that it would unfold and move into place perfectly the first time.
sentences.zh: 他们必须折叠遮阳罩，把所有东西装进火箭，并进行设计，以便一旦进入太空，它就能第一次完美地展开并移动到位。

sentences.en: So you can kind of see why it turned out to be a little bit harder than NASA thought at firSt.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以看出为什么它最终比NASA最初想象的要困难一些。

sentences.en: I mean, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我是说，是的，是的。

sentences.en: So originally, they thought they could get this done by 2007.
sentences.zh: 所以最初，他们认为可以在2007年完成。

sentences.en: And every time that you would look at the project, they were like, oh, the launch day is now pushed back 2010.
sentences.zh: 每次你查看这个项目时，他们都会说，哦，发射日期现在推迟到2010年了。

sentences.en: The price tag is now $3 billion.
sentences.zh: 价格标签现在是30亿美元。

sentences.en: And things were so bad that in 2011, they had to basically get a hard reset.
sentences.zh: 情况非常糟糕，以至于在2011年，他们基本上不得不进行一次彻底的重置。

sentences.en: And at that point, they said, we are now aiming for 2018.
sentences.zh: 在那一点上，他们说，我们现在的目标是2018年。

sentences.en: And we're going to say, this is going to cost no more than $8 billion, which is huge because, again, they thought it was $1 billion and changed when they started.
sentences.zh: 我们要说的是，这项目的成本不会超过80亿美元，这数额巨大，因为他们刚开始时以为只要10亿多美元。

sentences.en: And it's hard to overstate how important this was for NASA.
sentences.zh: 很难夸大这对NASA有多重要。

sentences.en: This was the signature program that was going to find NASA for decades to come.
sentences.zh: 这是未来几十年定义NASA的标志性项目。

sentences.en: And now NASA had to go back to Congress saying, oops, we can't get this done on time.
sentences.zh: 现在NASA不得不回到国会说，抱歉，我们没法按时完成。

sentences.en: And we're going to have to ask for another few billion dollars from you.
sentences.zh: 我们还得再向你们申请几十亿美元。

sentences.en: So with all these problems and the rising price tag, there was grumblings in Congress that maybe we should just cut our losses and cancel web.
sentences.zh: 所以面对这些问题和不断上涨的成本，国会里出现了抱怨声，觉得或许我们该止损，取消韦伯望远镜项目。

sentences.en: But in the end, Congress decided not to cancel web.
sentences.zh: 但最终，国会决定不取消韦伯项目。

sentences.en: It gave NASA additional money.
sentences.zh: 它给了NASA额外的资金。

sentences.en: The project started moving forward again.
sentences.zh: 项目重新开始推进。

sentences.en: And that brings us to launch on Christmas Day 2021.
sentences.zh: 这就带我们来到了2021年圣诞节的发射现场。

sentences.en: You're looking at live footage of an Ariane 5 rocket in Karoo, French Guiana.
sentences.zh: 你们现在看到的是法属圭亚那库鲁阿丽亚娜5号火箭的现场画面。

sentences.en: At the very top of that extraordinary machine, we find the most ambitious space observatory ever built.
sentences.zh: 在那台非凡机器的最顶端，搭载着有史以来建造的最雄心勃勃的空间天文台。

sentences.en: Web is on this Ariane 5 rocket.
sentences.zh: 韦伯望远镜就在这枚阿丽亚娜5号火箭上。

sentences.en: It's a European rocket.
sentences.zh: 这是一枚欧洲火箭。

sentences.en: The launch pad is in French Guiana in South America.
sentences.zh: 发射台位于南美洲的法属圭亚那。

sentences.en: It's actually a good place to launch because it's closer to the equator.
sentences.zh: 实际上这是个很好的发射地点，因为它离赤道更近。

sentences.en: So when you're trying to get to space, if you're close to the equator, you can take advantage of the rotation of the Earth to add velocity to your rocket.
sentences.zh: 所以当你试图进入太空时，如果靠近赤道，就可以利用地球的自转来增加火箭的速度。

sentences.en: I will remember that next time I'm going to space.
sentences.zh: 下次我要去太空时会记住这一点的。

sentences.en: This is live coverage of the historic launch of the James Webb Space Telescope.
sentences.zh: 这是詹姆斯·韦伯空间望远镜历史性发射的现场直播。

sentences.en: So, first thing in the morning, there are literally astronomers around the world watching the live stream of this rocket, and they're all completely nervous.
sentences.zh: 所以，一大早，全世界的天文学家们都在观看这枚火箭的直播，他们全都非常紧张。

sentences.en: What I'm thinking about is really looking at the universe in new light.
sentences.zh: 我真正在想的是，以全新的视角观察宇宙。

sentences.en: We have never seen the universe, how Webb will show it to us.
sentences.zh: 我们从未见过韦伯将要向我们展示的那种宇宙。

sentences.en: This is something that they've been thinking about, dreaming about since the 90s.
sentences.zh: 这是他们从90年代起就一直在思考、梦想的事情。

sentences.en: And they're worried that there might have been some oversight, like the Hubble mirror not being quite right,
sentences.zh: 他们担心可能会有疏忽，就像哈勃望远镜的镜片当初出了点问题一样，

sentences.en: that something would go wrong that they could not fix because this was a million miles away.
sentences.zh: 担心会发生他们无法修复的故障，因为这东西远在一百万英里之外。

sentences.en: Out on the launch pad, everything is in great shape.
sentences.zh: 在发射台上，一切状态良好。

sentences.en: Don't let those clouds fool you.
sentences.zh: 别被那些云层骗了。

sentences.en: We are go for launch.
sentences.zh: 我们准备发射。

sentences.en: 5, 4, 3, 2, unité, top.
And we have engine start.
sentences.zh: 引擎启动。

sentences.en: And then lift off.
sentences.zh: 然后升空。

sentences.en: Elmage EAP, décollage.
sentences.zh: 助推器分离，起飞。

sentences.en: The launch was perfect.
sentences.zh: 发射非常完美。

sentences.en: Décollage, lift off from a tropical rainforest to the edge of time itself.
sentences.zh: 起飞，从热带雨林飞向时间本身的边缘。

sentences.en: James Webb begins a voyage back to the birth of the universe.
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯·韦伯开启了回溯宇宙诞生之初的旅程。

sentences.en: This is it.
sentences.zh: 就是现在。

sentences.en: We have witnessed and the confirmation that Ariane 5 has safely delivered Webb into space.
sentences.zh: 我们见证并确认了阿丽亚娜5号已将韦伯安全送入太空。

sentences.en: All I can say is good luck, Webb, and bring us incredible data from the deep universe.
sentences.zh: 我只能说，祝你好运，韦伯，带回来自深空宇宙的惊人数据吧。

sentences.en: And for most space missions, once a spacecraft reaches orbit, you usually get this big sigh of release because you feel like everything else is not going to be as complex.
sentences.zh: 对于大多数太空任务，一旦航天器进入轨道，你通常会松一口气，因为你会觉得剩下的部分不会那么复杂了。

sentences.en: But this wasn't true for Webb.
sentences.zh: 但这对韦伯来说并非如此。

sentences.en: The hard part was its mirror had to un-dack itself and snap into its final configuration.
sentences.zh: 最难的部分是它的镜片必须展开并锁定到最终配置。

sentences.en: The sun shield had to unfold and deploy.
sentences.zh: 遮阳罩必须展开并部署到位。

sentences.en: And NASA identified 344 what they called single-point failures.
sentences.zh: NASA确定了344个所谓的单点故障。

sentences.en: So if something didn't snap into place, there was no backup system.
sentences.zh: 所以如果某个部件没能卡入到位，就没有备份系统。

sentences.en: And all 344 things, they all worked.
sentences.zh: 而这344个环节，全部成功了。

sentences.en: It got to its final destination at the end of January.
sentences.zh: 它在1月底到达了最终目的地。

sentences.en: The instruments turned on.
sentences.zh: 仪器开启了。

sentences.en: Almost everything worked as well as NASA could have possibly hoped.
sentences.zh: 几乎一切的运行情况都达到了NASA所能期望的最好水平。

sentences.en: And all this preparation, all this calibration, all this testing, it all paid off.
sentences.zh: 所有的准备、校准和测试，这一切都得到了回报。

sentences.en: And by June, they were ready to start taking their first scientific measurements.
sentences.zh: 到了6月，他们准备开始进行首次科学测量。

sentences.en: And so far, Webb seems to be working better than promised.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，韦伯的表现似乎比承诺的还要好。

sentences.en: The microns were on.
sentences.zh: 微米波段已开启。

sentences.en: Yeah, I'm sure whoever was in charge of the mirrors made sure they checked every measurement 20 times.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我相信负责镜片的人肯定确保了每一项测量都检查了20遍。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·朗森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一个关于设计之爱及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night, you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you.
sentences.zh: 即使在我还在黑胶唱片时代做夜店DJ的时候，每天晚上，你都要带着300件最珍贵的宝贝去上班。

sentences.en: And you turned a DJ booth into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你会把DJ台变成一个鲜活的快闪博物馆，陈列着精美的50年历史的艺术品。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼出品的《重构者》吧。

sentences.en: I'm Wynna Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是刘温娜。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我负责编写《纽约时报》游戏中的《连接》游戏。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我还喜欢试图捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖斯基。

sentences.en: And I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我每天负责制作《拼字蜜蜂》和《字母盒》游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做联觉的东西。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像你们刚才听到的人们制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问nytimes.com/games开始玩吧。

sentences.en: So, Ken, as you told us, the James Webb is already starting to show us things that we've never seen before.
sentences.zh: 那么，肯，正如你告诉我们的，詹姆斯·韦伯已经开始向我们展示我们从未见过的事物了。

sentences.en: What else do we expect for it to show us?
sentences.zh: 我们还期待它向我们展示什么？

sentences.en: Space-plain to me.
sentences.zh: 给我科普一下。

sentences.en: So, again, what makes Webb special is that its mirror is so much bigger than Hubble's.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，韦伯的特别之处在于它的镜片比哈勃大得多。

sentences.en: And it's looking at this new part of the spectrum of light, the infrared, to look at the universe.
sentences.zh: 而且它正在观察光谱中一个新的部分——红外线，来观测宇宙。

sentences.en: And because it's looking at the infrared, they can see details that they couldn't see before.
sentences.zh: 正因为它在观察红外线，所以能看到以前看不到的细节。

sentences.en: That's why this image is so much more colorful, so much more detailed than what Hubble could do.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么这张图像比哈勃拍摄的要丰富多彩、细节丰富得多。

sentences.en: And another major thing that they're planning to do with Webb is to start looking and examining planets around other stars, what we call exoplanets.
sentences.zh: 韦伯计划做的另一件大事是开始观察和检查其他恒星周围的行星，也就是我们所说的系外行星。

sentences.en: Exoplanets.
sentences.zh: 系外行星。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Exoplanets, planets around other stars.
sentences.zh: 系外行星，其他恒星周围的行星。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So, back in the early 90s, we had yet to see a single planet around another star.
sentences.zh: 在90年代初，我们还没有见过任何一颗其他恒星周围的行星。

sentences.en: Everyone assumed, like, there's billions of stars.
sentences.zh: 每个人都认为，毕竟有数十亿颗恒星。

sentences.en: There must be planets around many, if not most of them.
sentences.zh: 其中很多，如果不是大多数的话，肯定有行星环绕。

sentences.en: But no one had actually identified any.
sentences.zh: 但没人真正发现过任何一颗。

sentences.en: And it wasn't until 1994 where people started discovering them.
sentences.zh: 直到1994年人们才开始发现它们。

sentences.en: And now, we now know thousands of them.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们已经知道有数千颗了。

sentences.en: What Webb can do.
sentences.zh: 韦伯能做什么？

sentences.en: Webb is great, but it actually can't see individual planets.
sentences.zh: 韦伯很棒，但它实际上无法直接看到单个行星。

sentences.en: But it can do this amazing analysis of a planet.
sentences.zh: 但它能对行星进行这种惊人的分析。

sentences.en: And this is kind of a trick.
sentences.zh: 这其实是一种技巧。

sentences.en: Because for certain planets, they occasionally pass in front of a star.
sentences.zh: 因为对于某些行星，它们偶尔会从恒星前面经过。

sentences.en: So, basically, you just have a little black dot.
sentences.zh: 所以，基本上，你只会看到一个小黑点。

sentences.en: But what happens is that the atmosphere of the planet blocks certain colors of the starlight.
sentences.zh: 但发生的情况是，行星的大气层会阻挡星光的某些颜色。

sentences.en: So, you can actually compare the colors of the starlight by itself versus what colors you see when there's a tiny planet in front of it.
sentences.zh: 所以，你可以比较恒星本身的光谱颜色，与当有一颗小行星在它前面时你看到的颜色。

sentences.en: And there's going to be slight differences.
sentences.zh: 会有细微的差异。

sentences.en: Because different molecules, they will block slightly different colors from the starlight.
sentences.zh: 因为不同的分子会阻挡星光中略有不同的颜色。

sentences.en: And from that, you can actually identify what the atmosphere of that planet can be.
sentences.zh: 由此，你实际上可以确定那颗行星的大气层可能是什么样的。

sentences.en: So, it's a planet that's about the size of Earth.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一颗大小和地球差不多的行星。

sentences.en: It passes in front of stars.
sentences.zh: 它从恒星前面经过。

sentences.en: We can start seeing, is there oxygen in there?
sentences.zh: 我们可以开始观察，那里有氧气吗？

sentences.en: Is there water?
sentences.zh: 有水吗？

sentences.en: Is there things that perhaps are evidence of life on that planet?
sentences.zh: 有没有可能是那颗行星上存在生命的证据？

sentences.en: So, basically, what this telescope does is not look at the exoplanets directly, but analyze the atmosphere around the planets,
sentences.zh: 所以，基本上，这个望远镜的作用不是直接观察系外行星，而是分析行星周围的大气层，

sentences.en: which can then basically see if there are things that could point to potential signs of life.
sentences.zh: 从而基本上能看出是否有迹象指向潜在的生命存在。

sentences.en: Yeah, so we now know there are these star systems, and some of them are pretty close, where there's planets.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们现在知道有这些恒星系统，其中一些离我们很近，而且有行星。

sentences.en: In fact, there's one called TRAPPIST-1.
sentences.zh: 事实上，有一个叫TRAPPIST-1的系统。

sentences.en: It's about 40 light years away, so not far at all.
sentences.zh: 它距离我们大约40光年，所以一点也不远。

sentences.en: And it has seven Earth-sized planets in orbit around it.
sentences.zh: 它有七颗地球大小的行星在绕着它运行。

sentences.en: It's a pretty small star, so the planets are actually pretty close to the star.
sentences.zh: 那是一颗相当小的恒星，所以行星离恒星其实很近。

sentences.en: And three of them are in what is known as the habitable zone.
sentences.zh: 其中三颗位于所谓的宜居带内。

sentences.en: That's where it's not too cold or not too hot.
sentences.zh: 也就是不太冷也不太热的地方。

sentences.en: And if it's not too hot, not too cold, maybe there's liquid water on it.
sentences.zh: 如果不太热也不太冷，也许上面有液态水。

sentences.en: If there's liquid water...
sentences.zh: 如果有液态水……

sentences.en: Using process of elimination.
sentences.zh: 使用排除法。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: We don't know any of this information now.
sentences.zh: 我们现在还不知道任何这些信息。

sentences.en: We just know it looks like it's about the size of Earth.
sentences.zh: 我们只知道它看起来大小和地球差不多。

sentences.en: But we don't know anything about the property of the atmosphere or what's on the planet.
sentences.zh: 但我们对大气层的性质或行星上有什么一无所知。

sentences.en: And with Webb, we can actually start exploring not just TRAPPIST-1, but start looking across
sentences.zh: 有了韦伯，我们不仅可以开始探索TRAPPIST-1，还可以开始观察

sentences.en: all these many stars and all the planets around these stars and start getting a sense of what is the range of planets that exist in our galaxy?
sentences.zh: 所有这些众多的恒星以及它们周围的行星，并开始了解我们银河系中存在的行星种类范围。

sentences.en: How different are they from Earth?
sentences.zh: 它们与地球有多大不同？

sentences.en: How common is something like Earth?
sentences.zh: 像地球这样的行星有多普遍？

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So it is not far-fetched to say that this telescope is the furthest we have gotten in terms of having a tool that can understand whether there is potential life on another planet.
sentences.zh: 所以说这个望远镜是我们目前在拥有能够了解另一颗行星上是否存在潜在生命工具方面走得最远的一步，这并不牵强。

sentences.en: I mean, in terms of something like microbes living on a planet, this is the tool that will start giving us hints about that question.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，就行星上是否存在微生物而言，这就是将开始为我们提供该问题线索的工具。

sentences.en: So how long do we expect the James Webb to be doing this kind of work?
sentences.zh: 那么我们预计詹姆斯·韦伯能做多久这种工作？

sentences.en: The original lifetime was they were aiming for 10 years.
sentences.zh: 最初的设计寿命目标是10年。

sentences.en: Because the launch went so perfectly, they didn't have to use very much propellant for getting the trajectory corrected as it went out to its final destination.
sentences.zh: 因为发射非常完美，他们在前往最终目的地的过程中不需要使用太多的推进剂来修正轨道。

sentences.en: They now say they have enough propellant to last at least 20 years.
sentences.zh: 他们现在说剩下的推进剂足够维持至少20年。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Now, of course, things in space, you never know what's out there.
sentences.zh: 当然，太空里的事情，你永远不知道会发生什么。

sentences.en: There's rocks just whizzing back and forth in the solar system.
sentences.zh: 太阳系里到处都是飞来飞去的岩石。

sentences.en: And if one of them hits the telescope in the wrong spot, it could just knock it out of operation tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 如果其中一块击中了望远镜的关键部位，它明天就可能停止工作。

sentences.en: I mean, it actually has already been hit by one micrometeoroid that damaged one of the mirrors already.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它实际上已经被一颗微流星体击中过，已经损坏了一块镜片。

sentences.en: Already?
sentences.zh: 已经损坏了？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It happened a couple months ago.
sentences.zh: 那是几个月前发生的。

sentences.en: They sort of anticipated it.
sentences.zh: 他们其实预料到了这种情况。

sentences.en: It was a little bit bigger than what they were expecting, but they have ways to adjust for that.
sentences.zh: 虽然比他们预期的稍微大了一点，但他们有办法进行调整。

sentences.en: And they said it's still operating, meeting all of its specifications.
sentences.zh: 他们说它仍在运行，符合所有的技术指标。

sentences.en: Actually, they're actually hoping by measuring how many times it gets hit by different things, a better understanding of how much stuff there is in the solar system.
sentences.zh: 实际上，他们甚至希望通过测量它被不同物体撞击的次数，来更好地了解太阳系中有多少物质。

sentences.en: So even by being damaged...
sentences.zh: 所以即使在受损的情况下……

sentences.en: We even learn things when it gets hit.
sentences.zh: 我们甚至在它被撞击时也能学到东西。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So by being damaged, NASA learns more about the solar system.
sentences.zh: 所以通过受损，NASA对太阳系有了更多的了解。

sentences.en: If only I learned from damage.
sentences.zh: 我要是也能从受损中吸取教训就好了。

sentences.en: So can we now see this extraordinary scientific success from NASA?
sentences.zh: 那么我们现在能看到NASA这一非凡的科学成就了吗？

sentences.en: This telescope that is unique, launching to universal acclaim and excitement.
sentences.zh: 这台独特的望远镜在万众瞩目和兴奋中发射升空。

sentences.en: But as you said on the show before, it comes at a time in which it's been private companies and specifically billionaires who have been making the most hay in terms of space travel
sentences.zh: 但正如你之前在节目中所说，它出现的时机，正值私营公司，特别是亿万富翁们在太空旅行方面大出风头的时候，

sentences.en: in recent years, not NASA.
sentences.zh: 近年来是这样，而不是美国国家航空航天局（NASA）。

sentences.en: I'm thinking about SpaceX and Elon Musk travel.
sentences.zh: 我指的是SpaceX和埃隆·马斯克的旅行。

sentences.en: I'm thinking about Jeff Bezos and his brief space flight.
sentences.zh: 我指的是杰夫·贝索斯和他那次短暂的太空飞行。

sentences.en: How do we see James Webb and NASA's latest initiative in relationship with how these billionaires and
sentences.zh: 我们该如何看待詹姆斯·韦布望远镜和NASA的最新计划，以及这些亿万富翁和

sentences.en: how these private corporations have frankly changed our understanding of space travel?
sentences.zh: 这些私营公司如何坦率地改变了我们对太空旅行的理解？

sentences.en: So the billionaires are changing NASA.
sentences.zh: 所以，亿万富翁们正在改变NASA。

sentences.en: And I would say in many ways, that's a good thing in that it's more people going to space than have ever gone to space before.
sentences.zh: 我想说，在很多方面，这是一件好事，因为去太空的人比以往任何时候都多。

sentences.en: That's the human space flight part of NASA.
sentences.zh: 那是NASA载人航天的那一部分。

sentences.en: With Webb, this is the other side of NASA, the space part.
sentences.zh: 而韦布望远镜代表了NASA的另一面，即太空科学探索。

sentences.en: These are the things that NASA does that Elon Musk is never going to do.
sentences.zh: 这些是NASA在做，而埃隆·马斯克永远不会做的事情。

sentences.en: So...
sentences.zh: 所以……

sentences.en: This is science.
sentences.zh: 这是科学。

sentences.en: This is space science.
sentences.zh: 这是空间科学。

sentences.en: This is space science.
sentences.zh: 这是空间科学。

sentences.en: These are asking the fundamental questions that we all think about when we're up late at night and can't sleep.
sentences.zh: 这些是在探究我们深夜辗转反侧时都会思考的基本问题。

sentences.en: Are we alone?
sentences.zh: 我们是孤独的吗？

sentences.en: Why is there a universe at all?
sentences.zh: 为什么宇宙会存在？

sentences.en: These are questions that, you know, you can argue that this has no practical effect on your everyday life.
sentences.zh: 这些问题，你知道，你可以说它们对你的日常生活没有实际影响。

sentences.en: But those are the things that make people special, that we are curious.
sentences.zh: 但正是这些东西让人类变得特别，因为我们充满好奇心。

sentences.en: We wonder what's beyond the next hill.
sentences.zh: 我们想知道下一座山后面有什么。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗恒星后面有什么。

sentences.en: And it's just like centuries ago, people were exploring the oceans, exploring the new continents.
sentences.zh: 这就像几个世纪前，人们探索海洋、探索新大陆一样。

sentences.en: And NASA's exploring the solar system and the universe in ways that is very much in the adventure vein that people have always done.
sentences.zh: 而NASA正在以一种非常符合人类一贯冒险精神的方式探索太阳系和宇宙。

sentences.en: Well, I, for one, am deeply excited.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我个人感到非常兴奋。

sentences.en: Thank you, Ken, for teaching me and spicing up my wheat.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，肯，感谢你的教导，让我的生活变得丰富多彩。

sentences.en: It's good talking with you.
sentences.zh: 和你谈话很愉快。

sentences.en: After the break, Ken shares an update on what Webb has captured during its time in orbit.
sentences.zh: 休息之后，肯将分享韦布望远镜在轨道上拍摄到的最新成果。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: So, this Christmas marks the one-year anniversary of the launch of Webb.
sentences.zh: 今年圣诞节是韦布望远镜发射一周年纪念日。

sentences.en: It's been one year since NASA put this newest and most powerful telescope into space.
sentences.zh: 距离NASA将这台最新、最强大的望远镜送入太空已经过去一年了。

sentences.en: And Webb has continued to take amazing images better than almost anyone could have imagined.
sentences.zh: 韦布望远镜不断拍摄出令人惊叹的图像，效果几乎超出了所有人的想象。

sentences.en: It can capture up to 57 gigabytes of data per day.
sentences.zh: 它每天可以捕获高达57千兆字节的数据。

sentences.en: And as it's pure through every corner of the universe, it's allowed us to see some pretty amazing things.
sentences.zh: 随着它深入宇宙的每一个角落，它让我们看到了许多令人惊叹的事物。

sentences.en: So, one of the main parts of Webb's mission is to look at exoplanets, that is, planets around other stars.
sentences.zh: 韦布任务的主要部分之一是观测系外行星，也就是围绕其他恒星运行的行星。

sentences.en: And a few months ago, Webb captured its first image of an exoplanet.
sentences.zh: 几个月前，韦布拍摄了它的第一张系外行星图像。

sentences.en: It orbits a star 385 light-years from Earth in a constellation called Centaurus.
sentences.zh: 它围绕着一颗距离地球385光年的恒星运行，位于半人马座。

sentences.en: Because it's a giant ball of gas and because it's so far from its star, this particular exoplanet won't have life.
sentences.zh: 因为它是一个巨大的气态球体，而且距离恒星太远，这颗特定的系外行星不会有生命存在。

sentences.en: But it's the first step to studying these planets.
sentences.zh: 但这是研究这些行星的第一步。

sentences.en: Perhaps the most striking web image that we've seen so far has been the pillars of creation.
sentences.zh: 也许到目前为止我们看到的最引人注目的韦布图像是“创生之柱”。

sentences.en: A lot of people probably remember the one that Hubble took years ago.
sentences.zh: 很多人可能还记得哈勃望远镜多年前拍摄的那张照片。

sentences.en: It's these giant columns of gas in the Eagle Nebula, which is in the Milky Way.
sentences.zh: 那是鹰状星云中巨大的气体柱，位于银河系内。

sentences.en: And it's a place where stars are born.
sentences.zh: 那是恒星诞生的地方。

sentences.en: They almost look like the fingers of the hand of God reaching across the universe.
sentences.zh: 它们看起来几乎就像上帝之手伸向宇宙的手指。

sentences.en: Webb also took a picture of the pillar's creation.
sentences.zh: 韦布也拍摄了创生之柱的照片。

sentences.en: And that image is even more vivid and even more vibrant than what Hubble saw.
sentences.zh: 那张图像比哈勃看到的更加生动、更加鲜艳。

sentences.en: That's because Webb is looking at these longer wavelengths of light that are able to pierce the clouds of dust that block the light from Hubble.
sentences.zh: 这是因为韦布正在观测这些更长波长的光，它们能够穿透阻挡哈勃光线的尘埃云。

sentences.en: And because of this, astronomers can now see details and structures that were previously invisible to them.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，天文学家现在可以看到以前对他们来说不可见的细节和结构。

sentences.en: That could be filaments of dust and gas, or even stars.
sentences.zh: 那可能是尘埃和气体的丝状结构，甚至是恒星。

sentences.en: Webb has also found galaxies that until now were too far away and too dim to see.
sentences.zh: 韦布还发现了迄今为止太遥远、太暗淡而无法观测到的星系。

sentences.en: One of them is thought to have formed just 350 million years after the Big Bang.
sentences.zh: 其中一个被认为是在大爆炸后仅3.5亿年形成的。

sentences.en: And while 350 million years sounds like a really long time, the universe is almost 14 billion years old.
sentences.zh: 虽然3.5亿年听起来是很长的一段时间，但宇宙已经有近140亿年的历史了。

sentences.en: So in the grand scheme of things, these galaxies are among the first to light up the universe.
sentences.zh: 所以在宏观层面上，这些星系是宇宙中最早亮起来的星系之一。

sentences.en: If we think about the arc of space imagery, it's kind of like the history of television.
sentences.zh: 如果我们思考太空影像的发展历程，它有点像电视的历史。

sentences.en: Like how in the old days we had the equivalent of cathode ray Tvs.
sentences.zh: 就像过去我们有相当于阴极射线管电视的东西。

sentences.en: And then Hubble came along, it was like we finally got HD.
sentences.zh: 然后哈勃出现了，就像我们终于有了高清电视。

sentences.en: And now with Webb, we've got 4K, we've got WVision, we've got everything.
sentences.zh: 而现在有了韦布，我们有了4K，有了超高清，我们拥有了一切。

sentences.en: Everything scientists hope to be seeing, they are now seeing with Webb.
sentences.zh: 科学家们希望看到的一切，现在通过韦布都能看到了。

sentences.en: And this is just the beginning.
sentences.zh: 而这仅仅是个开始。

sentences.en: Today's episode was hosted by Astrid Herndon in conversation with science reporter Kenneth Chang.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由阿斯特丽德·赫恩登主持，与科学记者肯尼斯·张进行对话。

sentences.en: It was produced by Sidney Harper, Michael Simon-Johnson, Nina Feldman, Astha Chaturvedi, and Ricky Nevetsky,
sentences.zh: 节目由西德尼·哈珀、迈克尔·西蒙-约翰逊、尼娜·费尔德曼、阿斯塔·查图尔维迪和里奇·内维茨基制作，

sentences.en: and was edited by Michael Benoit, Patricia Willens, and Anita Bonadio, with help from Liz Balin.
sentences.zh: 由迈克尔·贝努瓦、帕特里夏·威伦斯和安妮塔·博纳迪奥剪辑，莉兹·巴林提供协助。

sentences.en: It contains original music by Marianne Lozano and Alicia Baitube, and was engineered by Chris Wood and Corey Shreppel.
sentences.zh: 节目包含玛丽安·洛萨诺和艾丽西亚·拜图贝的原创音乐，由克里斯·伍德和科里·施雷佩尔担任工程制作。

sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由Wonderly的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰兹伯格创作。

sentences.zh: 以上就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受到严密控制的机器运作。

sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.zh: 抱歉。

sentences.zh: 肃静。

sentences.zh: 我希望。
